MediaInfoFailed: Could not read the media info for this file.
MediaInfoNoFile: Nothing is playing, so there is no media to inspect.
PanelAbHint: Set A then B to loop that range.
ResetShortcutsDone: Shortcuts reset. Takes effect on the next launch.
SettingsHelpGpuApi: Which graphics interface renders the picture. Auto lets mpv pick the best fit and is recommended. d3d11 is the usual choice on Windows; vulkan has more features but also more driver trouble; opengl is the oldest fallback. A wrong value usually shows up as a black window or a failed start.
SettingsHelpGpuContext: Which window backend the API above runs on; normally chosen in pairs with it, such as d3d11 with win or vulkan with winvk. Auto lets mpv decide. A mismatch with the API gives a black window - set it back to auto to recover.
SettingsHelpScaleAntiring: Anti-ringing strength when enlarging (0-1). It softens the halo around edges at the cost of a slightly softer picture. 0 is off; around 0.75 is a common compromise.
SettingsHelpCscaleAntiring: Anti-ringing strength during chroma upscaling (0-1). Narrower in scope than the option above - it only affects colour edges.
SectionDescPlaybackSeekPreview: Thumbnail preview on the seek bar
SectionDescSubtitleFilter: Clean non-dialogue text out of accessibility subtitles
SettingsHelpSubFilterSdhHarder: Deletes bracketed text even when it reads like dialogue. Some releases wrap entire lines that way, which needs this on; if brackets appear legitimately in the dialogue, it will take them too.
SettingsHelpSubFilterSdh: Removes the hearing-impaired cues from SDH subtitles, such as [knocking] or [music]. They are recognised by their brackets, and anyone who can hear finds them noise.
SettingsHelpSubFilterSdhEnclosures: The characters treated as enclosing a sound description. The default, (),[],（）， is a round pair, a square pair and a full-width pair. Narrowing this avoids deleting brackets that are part of the dialogue.
SectionDescSubtitleSecondary: An extra track shown at the same time
SectionDescWindow: Always on top, resizing, aspect lock
SettingsAssociateFailed: Windows did not accept the file association. Check the log for details.
SettingsAssociatePackaged: This build is installed as an app package, so Windows takes the file list from the package manifest. Rebuild and reinstall the package to change it.
SettingsCheckForUpdatesDescription: Check the GitHub releases page for a newer version at startup.
SettingsCommandPlaceholder: Type an mpv command, e.g. set volume 60
SettingsConfigImported: Settings imported. Some options take effect on the next launch.
SettingsHelpOpenMpvConf: Open mpv.conf in your text editor. Lines here override the settings window — anything you write wins.
SettingsOpenMpvConfMissing: mpv.conf was not found. Launch the player once so it can create it.
SettingsControlBarCanvasHint: Drag the icons to reorder; drag off the bar to hide. The transport buttons are fixed.
SettingsCoverArtAlwaysScan: Scan cover art for any file
SettingsCustomizeHint: Reorder by dragging, rename, edit the raw mpv value, hide or restore each settings entry.
SettingsHelpAdLavcDownmix: Downmix multichannel audio to stereo at decoder level.
SettingsHelpAlwaysOnTop: Keep the player window above other windows.
SettingsHelpCursorAutohide: How long the pointer must stay still before it hides. Always hides it as soon as the picture appears; moving the mouse brings it back.
SettingsHelpCursorAutohideFsOnly: Hide the pointer only in fullscreen. In windowed mode it stays visible, which makes dragging and resizing easier.
SettingsHelpWindowBorder: Turning this off removes the border and shadow, which suits a small window parked in a corner.
SettingsHelpTitleBar: Hides the native title bar. The window's close button goes with it, so use a shortcut or the menu instead.
SettingsHelpAspectRatio: Force a display aspect ratio; Auto keeps the video's own ratio.
SettingsHelpAudioBuffer: Audio output buffer in seconds (0-10). 0 lets mpv choose (0.2 by default); larger reduces glitches but adds latency.
SettingsHelpAudioChannels: Speaker layout sent to the audio device; Auto (safe) falls back to a supported layout.
SettingsHelpAudioDelay: Audio delay in seconds. Negative values make audio earlier.
SettingsHelpAudioDevice: Audio output device name returned by mpv (e.g. auto or wasapi/...).
SettingsHelpAudioDisplay: What to show while playing audio: embedded cover art, external cover art, or nothing.
SettingsHelpAudioExclusive: WASAPI exclusive mode. Can reduce latency but blocks other apps from the device.
SettingsHelpAudioExts: Extensions treated as audio files for playlists, separated by commas.
SettingsHelpAudioFileAuto: Automatically load a matching external audio file next to the video.
SettingsHelpAudioFilePaths: Extra folders searched for matching external audio files, separated by semicolons.
SettingsHelpAudioFormat: Sample format used for audio output (Auto = leave mpv's default).
SettingsHelpAudioGapless: Keep the audio output open between files for gapless playback; Weak only keeps it between audio files.
SettingsHelpAudioLanguage: Preferred language for audio tracks; Auto matches the system language.
SettingsHelpAudioNormalizeDownmix: Normalize the downmixed audio when playing multichannel audio on stereo.
SettingsHelpAudioPitchCorrection: Keep the pitch when playback speed changes (otherwise speed-up raises the pitch).
SettingsHelpAudioReversalBuffer: Approximate max bytes buffered for backward decoding of audio.
SettingsHelpAudioSampleRate: Sample rate in Hz for audio output; 0 keeps mpv's default.
SettingsHelpAudioSpdif: Pass compressed audio (AC3/EAC3/DTS/TrueHD) through to the receiver without decoding. Leave Off for normal PCM output.
SettingsHelpAudioStreamSilence: Fill silent frames when there is no audio data (helps exclusive-mode output).
SettingsHelpAudioWaitOpen: How long mpv waits for audio output to open, in seconds. 0 uses mpv's default; usually only useful together with audio-stream-silence=yes.
SettingsHelpAutoCreatePlaylist: Automatically add files from the same folder to the playlist when opening a file.
SettingsHelpAutoWindowResize: Resize window on video resolution change.
SettingsHelpBackdrop: Background material of the main window. Both Mica and Acrylic support a custom tint in Custom theme mode.
SettingsHelpBackgroundTileColor0: The first checkerboard colour drawn behind the video where it is letterboxed or transparent. The pattern exists so you can tell 'outside the picture' apart from 'the picture is actually black' - which is why it is not plain black.
SettingsHelpBackgroundTileColor1: The second checkerboard colour, alternating with the first to form the visible pattern.
SettingsHelpBackgroundTileSize: Side length of each checkerboard square, in pixels. Small values make a fine grid that reads as noise; large values make the pattern obvious and the picture boundary clearer.
SettingsHelpBlendSubtitles: Draw subtitles into the video frame instead of overlaying them. Video limits subtitles to the visible picture.
SettingsHelpCacheEnabled: Network cache: Off disables, Auto caches only when needed, Yes always caches.
SettingsHelpCacheOnDisk: Buffer network streams to disk while playing, so seeking back does not re-download.
SettingsHelpCachePause: Pause playback while the network cache is filling. Disable to keep playing while buffering.
SettingsHelpCachePauseInitial: Enter buffering before starting playback to prefetch network data.
SettingsHelpCachePauseWait: Seconds of buffered data required before playback resumes after a stall.
SettingsHelpCacheSecs: Maximum seconds of network data kept in memory. 0 disables the limit.
SettingsHelpControlBarLayout: Choose a control bar style: original or centered. Click Customize to drag-reorder or hide icons, or use + to add them.
SettingsHelpCookiesFile: Netscape-format cookies file for sites that require login.
SettingsHelpCorrectDownscaling: Switches to a more precise colour conversion while reducing the video. Better quality, higher GPU cost - worth enabling the more you shrink.
SettingsHelpCoverArtAlwaysScan: Scan for cover art for any file type, not only audio files. Takes effect on the next start.
SettingsHelpCoverArtImageExts: Image extensions treated as cover art, separated by semicolons.
SettingsHelpCoverArtLoadFromFilesystem: Search the filesystem for cover art files. Takes effect on the next start.
SettingsHelpCoverArtNames: Cover art filenames to look for, separated by semicolons. Takes effect on the next start.
SettingsHelpCoverArtPreferEmbedded: Prefer the embedded cover-art track over an external cover image file.
SettingsHelpCoverArtPreload: Load cover art before playback starts. Takes effect on the next start.
SettingsHelpCscale: Chroma upscaling. A video stores colour at lower resolution than brightness, so it has to be filled back in before display - this is that step. It affects the sharpness of colour edges only; lines and shading belong to the upscaling algorithm above.
SettingsHelpCurlBufferSize: Producer-side ring buffer size that decouples the network thread (default 4 MiB).
SettingsHelpCurlConnectTimeout: TCP/TLS connect timeout; 0 uses libcurl defaults (default 30).
SettingsHelpCurlMaxRedirects: Maximum HTTP redirects to follow before reporting an error (default 16).
SettingsHelpCurlMaxRequestSize: Split seekable transfers into range requests of at most this size; 0 keeps one request.
SettingsHelpCurlMaxRetries: Transparent retry count for seekable transfers after recoverable errors (default 5).
SettingsHelpD3d11Adapter: Which GPU does the rendering, which matters on dual-GPU laptops where the integrated chip saves power and the discrete one performs better. The list holds the devices the system reported; empty lets the system choose, which is usually the right one. Picking the wrong GPU shows a black or frozen picture - set it back to empty to recover.
SettingsHelpD3d11ExclusiveFs: Uses exclusive fullscreen. It bypasses the desktop compositor for lower input lag, which matters if you care about responsiveness. The cost is slower window switching, and some devices or drivers simply go black or hang - if that happens, turn this off first.
SettingsHelpD3d11Flip: Uses the flip-model presentation path. On current Windows this is normally the best choice - fewer stutters and less tearing - so leave it on. Turn it off only if fullscreen stutters or freezes, which also makes this the first thing to try when display problems appear.
SettingsHelpD3d11OutputCsp: Which colour space D3D11 hands the picture to the system in. Empty means automatic, which follows the display's current SDR/WCG/HDR configuration and is the recommended setting. srgb is ordinary SDR, bt.2020 wide gamut, pq the HDR10 curve, linear for linear-light work. Specify it by hand only if the automatic choice comes out wrong.
SettingsHelpD3d11OutputFormat: Pixel format of the swap chain - the final buffer handed to the display. Empty is automatic and recommended. rgb10_a2 is 10-bit colour, which reduces banding on a 10-bit panel; rgba16f is more precise but uses more VRAM. On an ordinary 8-bit screen, leave it automatic.
SettingsHelpD3d11SyncInterval: Vertical sync: how many refresh cycles pass before a frame is presented. 1 is on - no tearing, at the cost of some latency. 0 is off - lowest latency, but horizontal tearing may appear. Going above 1 is usually a compromise when there is not enough performance.
SettingsHelpD3d11Warp: Renders in software (WARP) instead of on the GPU. It exists to diagnose graphics-driver trouble: if the picture is fine with it on and wrong with it off, the driver is the problem. Software rendering is very slow - choose No for normal viewing.
SettingsHelpDScale: The algorithm used to reduce the video - applied when the video is larger than the window. Bicubic is softer by default; Lanczos is sharper when shrinking a lot, such as 4K footage in a 1080p window.
SettingsHelpDeband: Removes the stair-step colour bands that appear in gradients, most visibly in skies and shadows. It works by adding fine noise to buy smoothness, so expect a little grain - and it disables hardware decoding, so turn it off if you rely on that.
SettingsHelpDebugLog: Write debug logs to %LOCALAPPDATA%\mpv-winui\logs. Useful when reporting issues.
SettingsHelpDeinterlace: Deinterlace interlaced video: Auto detects, Yes always, No never.
SettingsHelpDemuxerCacheDir: Folder for the on-disk demuxer cache. Leave empty to let mpv decide.
SettingsHelpDemuxerHysteresisSecs: Seconds the demuxer must exceed a cache range before switching back. 0 uses mpv's default.
SettingsHelpDemuxerMaxBackBytes: How much data the demuxer keeps buffered behind the current position. 0 disables the limit.
SettingsHelpDemuxerMaxBytes: How much data the demuxer keeps buffered for each stream. Larger values improve seeking back on network files but use more memory (default 150 MiB, recommended 1024 MiB).
SettingsHelpDemuxerReadahead: Seconds of data the demuxer reads ahead. Larger values help network streams but use more memory.
SettingsHelpDirectoryFilterTypes: File types collected for the playlist when a folder is opened: video,audio,image,archive,playlist.
SettingsHelpDirectoryMode: How subfolders are handled when opening a directory: lazy adds on demand, recursive adds everything.
SettingsHelpDisplayPeak: The display's peak brightness in nits (0-10000). 0 detects it automatically, falling back to 1000 when the display reports nothing. It is used both to judge whether the screen counts as HDR and, when target peak is 0, as the tone-mapping target. Setting it above the real value darkens the picture and clips highlights.
SettingsHelpDither: Adds dithering during colour-depth conversion: fine noise stands in for colour levels the display cannot show, which keeps gradients from banding. The default is right for most setups.
SettingsHelpDitherDepth: Target bit depth for the dithered output. Auto matches the source; pick 8 for an 8-bit display, or try 10 on a 10-bit panel. Going above what the screen can show gains nothing.
SettingsHelpExportConfig: Save all settings to a settings file.
SettingsHelpFileAssociations: Choose which formats should open with this player. Changes apply immediately.
SettingsHelpGamutMappingMode: What happens to colours the display cannot show. clip snaps them to the nearest displayable colour - fastest, but neighbouring shades merge into flat patches. desaturate pulls their saturation down until they fit, which looks the most natural (the default). warn just highlights out-of-range areas for troubleshooting. darken darkens them into range.
SettingsHelpGlslShaderOpts: Values passed to shaders that expose tunable parameters, written name=value and separated by commas, for example param1=2,param2=0.5. The shader itself defines the names; an unknown one is silently ignored rather than reporting an error, so add one at a time and watch the result.
SettingsHelpGlslShaders: GLSL shader files layered onto the picture, with arrows setting the order - order matters, since each one works on the previous result. Disabled entries stay in the list but do nothing. Shaders change the look drastically, so check the result after adding each one.
SettingsHelpGlslShadersAppend: Extra shader files loaded at startup, separated by semicolons, for example ~~/shaders/a.glsl;D:/mpv/b.glsl where ~~/ is mpv's config directory. Unlike the list above, entries written here never appear in that list and are not touched by the UI.
SettingsHelpGpuShaderCache: Stores compiled shaders on disk so later launches read them instead of recompiling. It affects startup time only, never the picture; changing a shader triggers a recompile.
SettingsHelpGpuShaderCacheDir: Where the compiled-shader cache is stored. Leave it empty for the built-in default, the mpv folder under your app data directory. Fill it in only to move the cache to another drive.
SettingsHelpHdrAutoLog: Writes the RTX Video HDR detection steps to hdr_auto.log, for working out why it did not engage. The log keeps growing, so turn it off once you are done. Takes effect on the next launch.
SettingsHelpHdrAutoMode: RTX Video HDR, NVIDIA only: converts SDR content to HDR in real time so older material looks more vivid on an HDR screen. Auto enables it only when an HDR display is detected; On forces it; Off disables it. Needs a recent driver and an RTX card.
SettingsHelpHdrComputePeak: Where the peak brightness figure comes from. Auto lets mpv decide. Yes measures the actual peak of each frame, which is more accurate but costs performance and makes overall brightness drift with the content. No trusts the metadata in the file, which is cheapest but often wrong.
SettingsHelpHdrContrastRecovery: Restores some of the contrast that tone mapping flattened, as a fraction: 0 is off, 1 gives back 100 % (the default). Lower it for content that is already very contrasty, or highlights will blow out.
SettingsHelpHdrContrastSmoothness: How strongly the contrast recovery is smoothed (default 50). Lower follows the picture more closely but can flicker or halo at the boundary between bright and dark; on a small or low-DPI screen, lower is better.
SettingsHelpHdrOverrideMode: Overrides the app's automatic detection of the display's HDR capability. Auto follows the app (default); forcing HDR or SDR suits a wrong detection, or pinning one output. **Takes effect on the next launch**, so restart the player after changing it.
SettingsHelpHdrPeakDecayRate: How fast the tracked peak brightness falls, in dB per second (default 20). Low values remember longer - steady, but slow to react when a scene really does get darker. High values follow faster, at the cost of brightness constantly drifting. Only meaningful when peak detection is set to Yes.
SettingsHelpHdrSceneThresholdHigh: The upper threshold, in dB (default 10). A difference above this is treated as a certain scene change, so it sets how hard the reset is to trigger by accident: raising it makes detection more conservative, resetting only on obvious cuts.
SettingsHelpHdrSceneThresholdLow: The lower threshold, in dB (default 5), for deciding a new scene has started. When the brightness difference between consecutive frames exceeds it, peak detection resets. Lowering it makes the trigger easier to hit, so small shifts in dark scenes start counting as cuts.
SettingsHelpHrSeek: High-resolution seeking. On can be slower but more accurate.
SettingsHelpHrSeekFramedrop: Allow dropping video frames while seeking for faster response.
SettingsHelpHttpHeaderFields: Comma-separated HTTP header fields, e.g. 'Field1: value1','Field2: value2'.
SettingsHelpHttpProxy: HTTP/HTTPS proxy URL. Must start with http://; not used for https URLs.
SettingsHelpHwdec: Hardware decoding API. Auto is recommended; Off uses software decoding (some video filters only work reliably in software).
SettingsHelpHwdecCodecs: Codecs that may use hardware decoding. All tries every codec; set a comma list such as h264,hevc to limit it.
SettingsHelpIcc3dlutSize: Resolution used when converting an ICC profile into a 3D lookup table (Auto / 64³ / 128³ / 256³). A larger table maps colour more accurately but converts more slowly and uses more VRAM. Auto balances the two; leave it unless you are chasing maximum colour accuracy.
SettingsHelpIccCache: Stores the ICC-to-3D-LUT conversion on disk so later launches read it instead of converting again. It affects startup time only, never the picture.
SettingsHelpIccCacheDir: Where the conversion cache above is stored. Leave it empty for the built-in default, the mpv folder under your app data directory. Fill it in only to put the cache on another drive or at a fixed path.
SettingsHelpIccForceContrast: Forces the static contrast ratio mpv assumes for the display, in nits (0-1000000; 0 means no forcing). OLED owners commonly enter 1000000, because those panels switch pixels fully off and the black really is black, which makes ICC colour correction more accurate. Do not copy that onto an LCD, or shadows get crushed.
SettingsHelpIccProfile: Path to a specific ICC profile to load (.icc or .icm). Empty uses the one the system has assigned to the current display, which is usually what you want. Fill it in only to use a particular calibration file.
SettingsHelpIccProfileAuto: Loads the ICC profile the system has assigned to the current display and corrects colours with it. Turning it off skips ICC correction entirely, so the picture goes out in the panel's native colours. To use the specific profile path above, turn this off first.
SettingsHelpImageDisplayDuration: How long each image stays on screen in slideshow/directory mode, in seconds.
SettingsHelpImageExts: Extensions treated as images for playlists, separated by commas.
SettingsHelpImageSubsHdrPeak: Peak white brightness of image subtitles (PGS etc.) when the output is HDR.
SettingsHelpImageSubsVideoResolution: Use the video resolution for image subtitles instead of the stored resolution.
SettingsHelpImportConfig: Restore settings from a settings file.
SettingsHelpInputIme: Enable the Windows input method editor for text fields.
SettingsHelpInputIpcServer: Named pipe for external programs to control mpv. Leave empty to disable.
SettingsHelpInterpolation: Frame interpolation: generates in-between frames so fast pans and ghosting look smoother. It gives the 'soap opera' look, needs spare GPU and VRAM, and only takes effect once the sync mode above is set to display-resample.
SettingsHelpInverseToneMapping: Inverse tone mapping: expands SDR content upward into HDR so older material gets more dynamic range on an HDR screen. It is an educated guess rather than a restoration, not every tone-mapping curve supports it, and results vary by source - try it on a few clips first.
SettingsHelpKeepOpen: Keep the window open after the playlist ends instead of quitting.
SettingsHelpLanguage: Language of the settings UI, menu bar and right-click menus. Applies immediately.
SettingsHelpLinearDownscaling: Reduces in linear light for more accurate colour detail, at the cost of a slightly softer, greyer picture overall. Only matters when the video is being shrunk.
SettingsHelpLinearUpscaling: Enlarges in linear light, so colours blend the way light physically does - gradients and semi-transparent areas look more natural. The cost is that dark areas can look washed out. Mutually exclusive with sigmoid upscaling - pick one.
SettingsHelpLoopPlaylist: Repeat the playlist after the last file (Off / infinite / force).
SettingsHelpMetadataOsdAutohideForAudio: Automatically hide the metadata overlay after the timeout for audio files.
SettingsHelpMetadataOsdAutohideForAudioW: Automatically hide the metadata overlay after the timeout for audio files displayed with album art.
SettingsHelpMetadataOsdAutohideStatusTim: Seconds before the status OSD hides automatically. Takes effect on the next start.
SettingsHelpMetadataOsdAutohideTimeout: Seconds before the metadata OSD hides automatically.
SettingsHelpMetadataOsdEnableForAudio: Show the metadata overlay for audio files.
SettingsHelpMetadataOsdEnableForAudioWit: Show the metadata overlay for audio files displayed with album art.
SettingsHelpMetadataOsdEnableForImage: Show the metadata OSD for image files too. Takes effect on the next start.
SettingsHelpMetadataOsdEnableForVideo: Show the metadata OSD for video files too. Takes effect on the next start.
SettingsHelpMetadataOsdEnabled: Show the metadata OSD (artist, album, title) when playback starts. No metadata OSD is shown when disabled. Takes effect on the next start.
SettingsHelpMetadataOsdMessageMaxLength: Maximum length of metadata OSD messages in characters. Takes effect on the next start.
SettingsHelpMetadataOsdShowAlbumTrack: Show the album track number in the metadata OSD. Takes effect on the next start.
SettingsHelpMetadataOsdShowChapter: Show the current chapter number in the metadata OSD. Takes effect on the next start.
SettingsHelpNetworkTimeout: Network request timeout in seconds; 0 uses FFmpeg defaults (default 60).
SettingsHelpOsdAlignX: Horizontal position of OSD text: left, center or right.
SettingsHelpOsdAlignY: Vertical position of OSD text: top, center or bottom.
SettingsHelpOsdBarHeight: Height of the seek/volume progress bar, as a percentage of the screen.
SettingsHelpOsdBarWidth: Width of the seek/volume progress bar, as a percentage of the screen.
SettingsHelpOsdBlur: Gaussian blur applied to OSD text (0 disables).
SettingsHelpOsdBackColor: The fill behind OSD text, semi-transparent black by default. It is what keeps the OSD readable over busy pictures; making it fully transparent leaves only the outline and shadow.
SettingsHelpOsdMarginYOffset: Moves the OSD up or down from where it normally sits (positive is upward). Use it to dodge one part of the picture without changing the margins.
SettingsHelpOsdSelectedColor: Colour of the highlighted item in mpv's own OSD lists, amber by default. Only visible when an mpv OSD menu is in use, such as chapters or the playlist.
SettingsHelpOsdSelectedOutlineColor: Outline colour of that highlighted item's text, black by default. It is what keeps the letters legible on a bright highlight.
SettingsHelpOsdDuration: How long on-screen messages stay visible (milliseconds).
SettingsHelpOsdFont: Font used for on-screen messages. Defaults to the system font.
SettingsHelpOsdFontSize: Font size of on-screen messages, relative to the screen height.
SettingsHelpOsdFractions: Show time values with millisecond precision.
SettingsHelpOsdScale: Scales the whole OSD on top of the font size (default 1). After moving to a bigger screen the OSD looks small; this grows everything at once instead of each size field.
SettingsHelpOsdScaleByWindow: Lets the OSD grow and shrink with the window (on by default). Keeps it from looking oversized in a small window, and enlarges it again in fullscreen.
SettingsHelpOsdBold: Draws OSD text bold, which reads better over a bright picture. Matters most at small sizes or on a high-DPI screen.
SettingsHelpOsdItalic: Draws OSD text italic. A font without a true italic gets skewed instead, which can look slightly muddy.
SettingsHelpOsdJustify: How multi-line OSD text is aligned. Auto decides from the content; pinning left or right stops long filenames from jumping around as they wrap.
SettingsHelpOsdSpacing: Extra space between OSD characters, positive or negative (default 0). A small positive value helps when the font sets them too tightly.
SettingsHelpOsdFontsDir: Where the OSD looks for extra fonts. Only needed to render the OSD in a font the system does not have. Note that ASS subtitles search the same place.
SettingsHelpOsdFontProvider: Where OSD fonts come from. Auto picks the sensible option for the platform; Fontconfig suits a system with its own fontconfig setup; None falls back to built-in fonts only. A wrong choice usually shows up as boxes instead of letters.
SettingsHelpOsdShaper: How the OSD font turns characters into glyphs. Complex (the default) renders joined scripts such as Arabic and Devanagari correctly; simple costs less. For Latin and CJK it makes no difference.
SettingsHelpOsdShadowOffset: Distance of the drop shadow behind OSD text (default 0, off). It is a different readability aid from the outline: the outline rings the glyph, the shadow darkens one side, which reads more like print.
SettingsHelpOsdLevel: Amount of OSD information mpv shows: 0 hides everything, 3 shows the most.
SettingsHelpOsdMarginX: Horizontal distance of OSD text from the screen edge, in pixels.
SettingsHelpOsdMarginY: Vertical distance of OSD text from the screen edge, in pixels.
SettingsHelpOsdOnSeek: What to show while seeking: progress bar, message, both, or nothing. Message is recommended.
SettingsHelpOsdPlayingMsg: Message shown on the OSD when a file starts playing. Supports ${filename} etc.
SettingsHelpOsdPlayingMsgDuration: How long the playback-start message stays visible (milliseconds). 0 uses the global OSD duration.
SettingsHelpOverrideDisplayFps: Forces the display refresh rate mpv assumes, for when the system reports it wrongly - a panel driven at 59.94 Hz but announced as 60. 0 means no override. Fractions are allowed: 1000/1001 is exactly 59.94.
SettingsHelpPanscan: Crop/zoom amount used to fill the screen and remove black bars (0-1).
SettingsHelpPiP: Switch the window to a compact always-on-top mini player.
SettingsHelpPiPAnchor: Screen corner the mini player claims when it opens.
SettingsHelpPiPAspectRatioLock: Keep the video aspect ratio while resizing the mini player. Turn off to stretch it freely.
SettingsHelpPiPControls: Show the control bar (volume, play, seek) when the pointer moves to the bottom of the mini-player.
SettingsHelpPiPOpacity: Opacity of the picture-in-picture window (0.2-1.0). Applies the next time it opens.
SettingsHelpPiPTopButtons: Show the back and exit buttons when the pointer moves to the top of the mini-player.
SettingsHelpPrefetchPlaylist: Start loading the next playlist entry while the current one still plays.
SettingsHelpReferrer: Referrer path or URL for HTTP requests. Leave empty to send none.
SettingsHelpRememberWindowSize: Save the window size and position on exit and restore them on the next launch.
SettingsHelpReplaygain: Apply ReplayGain loudness normalization. Track uses per-track, Album uses per-album gain tags.
SettingsHelpResumePlayback: Restore the last playback position on startup.
SettingsHelpSavePositionOnQuit: Remember the playback position when quitting so the file can resume later.
SettingsHelpScale: The algorithm used to enlarge the video - applied when the video is smaller than the window. Lanczos balances quality and speed; EWA Lanczos is sharper but costs more GPU. Keep the default if unsure.
SettingsHelpScreenshotAvifEncoder: AV1 encoder used for AVIF screenshots.
SettingsHelpScreenshotHighBitDepth: Preserve high bit depth in screenshots. Can produce very large files.
SettingsHelpScreenshotJpegSourceChroma: Use the source video's chroma subsampling in JPEG screenshots.
SettingsHelpScreenshotJxlDistance: JXL visual distance: 0 is lossless, higher values compress more.
SettingsHelpScreenshotJxlEffort: JPEG XL encode effort (1-9); higher is slower but smaller.
SettingsHelpScreenshotPngCompression: PNG compression level (0-9). Higher saves space but costs time.
SettingsHelpScreenshotPngFilter: PNG compression filter preset (0 none, 5 best compression).
SettingsHelpScreenshotSw: Capture screenshots through the software path. More compatible with some GPUs, but slower.
SettingsHelpScreenshotTagColorspace: Tag the screenshot with the correct color space when the format supports it.
SettingsHelpScreenshotTemplate: Filename template. %F filename, %P time, %n counter, %w/%h size, %f format.
SettingsHelpScreenshotWebpCompression: WebP compression level (0-6); higher compresses better but is slower.
SettingsHelpSeekHold: Keep the window size fixed while seeking so filter reattachment does not resize the window.
SettingsHelpShowOsdPlayingMsg: Show a message on the OSD when a file starts playing. Off hides it.
SettingsHelpSigmoidUpscaling: Applies an S-shaped curve before enlarging, which tones down near-white and near-black so edges stop glowing (ringing). The cost is a slightly flatter, greyer picture. Mutually exclusive with linear-light upscaling - pick one.
SettingsHelpSpeed: Playback speed saved for the next launch (1.0 is normal).
SettingsHelpAbLoopA: Start of the A-B repeat range. 0 means this end is not set.
SettingsHelpAbLoopB: End of the A-B repeat range. The loop starts once both ends are set.
SettingsHelpAbLoopCount: How many times the A-B range repeats before playback continues. -1 repeats forever.
SettingsHelpStartFullscreen: Enter fullscreen immediately when the player starts.
SettingsHelpStartMaximized: Open the window maximized on launch.
SettingsHelpStretchImageSubsToScreen: Stretch image subtitles (e.g. PGS) to the screen resolution so they can render in the black margins.
SettingsHelpSubAlignX: Horizontal position of subtitles: left, center or right.
SettingsHelpSubAlignY: Vertical position of subtitles: top, center or bottom.
SettingsHelpSubAssForceMargins: Force ASS subtitles into the black margins when available.
SettingsHelpSubAssOverride: How strongly ASS/SSA subtitle styles are overridden. Scale (recommended) keeps layout; Strip removes styles and Force may break styled effects.
SettingsHelpSubAssScaleWithWindow: Scale ASS subtitles with the window size instead of the video size.
SettingsHelpSubAssStyleOverrides: Override ASS style values, e.g. Fontname=Microsoft YaHei. Leave empty to keep file styles.
SettingsHelpSubAssUseVideoData: Video stream information passed to libass. All matches VSFilter behavior.
SettingsHelpSubAssVideoAspectOverride: Override the video aspect ratio reported to libass for ASS rendering.
SettingsHelpSubAssVsfilterColorCompat: How ASS subtitle colors are converted for compatibility with VSFilter.
SettingsHelpSubAuto: Automatically load a matching external subtitle file next to the video.
SettingsHelpSubClearOnSeek: Hide text subtitles while seeking (older subtitle libraries may misbehave).
SettingsHelpSubCodePage: Character encoding of text subtitle files; Auto detects it.
SettingsHelpSubColor: Text subtitle color as #RRGGBB or #AARRGGBB. Leave empty for the file default.
SettingsHelpSubDelay: Shift subtitles earlier or later, in seconds.
SettingsHelpSubBitmapMaxSize: Largest decoded size allowed for bitmap subtitles such as PGS and VobSub; 0 means no limit (the default). Lowering it stops huge graphics subtitles eating VRAM, at the cost of those subtitles not showing at all.
SettingsHelpSubAssPruneDelay: How long off-screen ASS events are kept before being discarded, in seconds (-1 keeps them forever, the default). Keeping them makes scrolling smoother; complex effects then hold memory.
SettingsHelpSubAssJustify: Justifies multi-line ASS subtitles instead of centring each line. Dialogue that was laid out with spaces looks better; effects subtitles that position with spaces can shift.
SettingsHelpSubMarginYOffset: Moves subtitles up or down from where they normally sit (positive is upward). Use it to nudge them without changing the margins.
SettingsHelpSubOutlineColor: Colour of the outline around subtitle text, black by default. It is what separates the letters from a bright background. ASS subtitles carry their own styling and ignore this.
SettingsHelpSubSpacing: Extra space between letters, positive or negative (default 0). A small positive value helps when a font sets them too tightly.
SettingsHelpSubScale: Scales subtitles on top of whatever size the font already asks for (default 1). Use it when a release ships small text, or after moving to a bigger screen.
SettingsHelpSubGauss: Blurs subtitle edges with a Gaussian (0-3; 0 is off). Softens the letterforms. Higher values get visibly fuzzy and harder to read.
SettingsHelpSubShaper: How the subtitle font turns characters into glyphs. Complex (the default) handles joined scripts such as Arabic and Devanagari; simple is faster but renders those wrongly. For Latin and CJK it makes no difference.
SettingsHelpSubForcedEventsOnly: Within one track, show only the events marked forced - the ones translating foreign dialogue. Useful for watching a foreign film with the original audio.
SettingsHelpSubsFallbackForced: What to do when the two rules above find nothing: no subtitles, forced ones only, or any subtitle at all.
SettingsHelpSubsWithMatchingAudio: Only auto-select a subtitle whose language matches the audio. Forced only restricts this to forced tracks. Stops an English dub picking up English subtitles.
SettingsHelpSubsMatchOsLanguage: When picking a subtitle track automatically, prefer the one matching the interface language. Saves picking by hand on releases with several tracks.
SettingsHelpSubFixTiming: Repairs badly authored subtitles: entries that overlap or flash by too fast are adjusted until they are readable. Helpful for sloppy releases, harmless for clean ones.
SettingsHelpSubFixTimingThreshold: Two subtitles are only merged when they are closer than this many milliseconds (default 210). Lower it to be more conservative and only touch clear overlaps.
SettingsHelpSubVisibility: Master switch for subtitles. Turning it off still loads subtitle files, it just stops drawing them.
SettingsHelpSecondarySubDelay: Shifts only the second track's timing; positive delays it. Use it to line the two tracks up when they disagree.
SettingsHelpSecondarySubPos: Vertical position of the second track, where 100 sits at the bottom. A value above the main subtitle keeps the two from overlapping.
SettingsHelpSecondarySubScale: Scale of the second track relative to the main one. 1 means the same size.
SettingsHelpSecondarySubVisibility: Master switch for the second subtitle track. The file has to carry one for the selected subtitle - common with bilingual releases.
SettingsHelpSecondarySubAssOverride: Whether the second track applies ASS styling. Match it to the main subtitle's setting so the two are handled the same way; otherwise they can look inconsistent.
SettingsHelpSubEmbeddedFonts: Use fonts embedded in the media container (e.g. MKV).
SettingsHelpSubFallback: What mpv does when no subtitle track matches the preferred language.
SettingsHelpSubFilePaths: Extra folders searched for matching external subtitle files, separated by semicolons.
SettingsHelpSubFont: Font family name used for subtitles. Leave empty for the default font.
SettingsHelpSubFontFile: Pick a folder; mpv scans it for extra subtitle fonts (sub-fonts-dir), then choose the family in Subtitle font.
SettingsHelpSubFontProvider: Font provider used for subtitle fonts. Auto is recommended; Fontconfig enables system font fallback.
SettingsHelpSubHdrPeak: Peak white brightness of text subtitles when the output is HDR. SDR equals about 203 nits.
SettingsHelpSubHinting: Font hinting for subtitle text: none, light, normal or native (may misposition text).
SettingsHelpSubJustify: Horizontal alignment of subtitle text: auto, left, center or right.
SettingsHelpSubLineSpacing: Extra spacing between subtitle lines (can be negative).
SettingsHelpSubMarginX: Horizontal distance of subtitles from the screen edge, in pixels.
SettingsHelpSubMarginY: Vertical distance of subtitles from the screen edge, in pixels.
SettingsHelpSubPos: Vertical subtitle position: 100 is the bottom edge, 0 the top edge.
SettingsHelpSubScaleByWindow: Scale subtitle text together with the video window.
SettingsHelpSubScaleSigns: Scale symbols and signs in subtitles with the font.
SettingsHelpSubShadowOffset: Offset of the subtitle shadow, in pixels.
SettingsHelpSubUseMargins: Render text subtitles in the black margins when available.
SettingsHelpSubtitleLanguage: Preferred language for subtitle tracks; Auto matches the system language.
SettingsHelpTargetColorspaceHint: Switches the output colour space to match whatever is playing. With it on, an HDR file switches the output to HDR and an SDR file switches it back, so you are not changing it by hand. Recommended if you want HDR passthrough - letting the TV or monitor do its own mapping.
SettingsHelpTargetColorspaceHintMode: Which information the automatic switch goes by. target uses only the values you set here. source uses the colour space the file declares (the default, and the closest match to the content). source-dynamic uses the per-second dynamic metadata, which is more accurate only when the file actually carries it.
SettingsHelpTargetColorspaceHintStrict: Keeps output strictly inside the target colour space instead of adapting to the file's gamut. On, colours beyond the target are mapped in regardless - more consistent, possibly duller. Off lets the output widen to follow the source.
SettingsHelpTargetGamut: Restricts output to a named colour gamut. Enter a colour space name such as bt.709 (ordinary SDR), bt.2020 or display-p3; leave it empty to use the metadata in the file. Only useful when you deliberately want to force a gamut - a wrong value shows up as an obvious colour shift.
SettingsHelpTargetPeak: The target brightness for tone mapping, in nits (0-10000) - how bright the brightest part of the picture should actually be. 0 uses the display peak value above (the default). Only set it manually if you know your screen's peak better than mpv does, or deliberately want to cap brightness.
SettingsHelpTargetPrim: The display's primaries - the exact positions of red, green and blue in colour space, which decide how wide a range of colour the screen can show. Without an ICC profile loaded, this tells mpv which set your screen uses: bt.709 for an ordinary SDR panel, bt.2020 for wide-gamut/HDR, display-p3 common on Apple hardware and some laptops. Empty follows what the display reports.
SettingsHelpTargetTrc: The display's transfer curve - how a brightness number maps to actual light output. pq is the HDR one (HDR10, Dolby Vision). srgb and gamma2.2 are the usual curves for SDR panels and are very close to each other. linear is for linear-light processing. Empty follows what the display reports.
SettingsHelpTestMpvCommandLog: Write every command sent to mpv to the app log for troubleshooting.
SettingsHelpTestOsdMessage: Turn on to display a test OSD message; it resets immediately.
SettingsHelpTestSignal: Play a test signal for debugging audio output.
SettingsHelpTheme: Choose the color theme. Auto follows the Windows app mode and does not copy the accent color.
SettingsHelpThemeAccentColor: Tint color for the backdrop material. Used by the Custom theme; the other themes follow the system accent automatically.
SettingsHelpThemeLuminosity: Strength of a white/black layer laid over the backdrop: 50 is neutral, higher brightens toward solid white, lower darkens toward solid black.
SettingsHelpThemeOpacity: How transparent the window backdrop material is (100 = fully transparent).
SettingsHelpThumbnailInterval: How often the preview refreshes while hovering, in milliseconds. Larger values save CPU on big files.
SettingsHelpThumbnailSize: Width of the seek-bar preview thumbnail. Applies the next time the preview initializes, e.g. after reopening a file.
SettingsHelpTlsVerify: Verify HTTPS peer certificates. Only disable for known-good reasons such as corporate proxies.
SettingsHelpToneMapping: The algorithm that brings HDR brightness back down to something an SDR screen can show. It only applies when the source is HDR and the display is not. BT.2390 is the accepted all-round choice; try BT.2446a if a dim screen looks washed out; Clip keeps the most detail but flattens highlights outright.
SettingsHelpToneMappingMaxBoost: The most tone mapping is allowed to brighten the picture (1-10, default 1). Raising it lifts shadows further, at the risk of a washed-out, greyish look with no real black; increase it in small steps and only if the picture really is too dark.
SettingsHelpToneMappingVisualize: A debug overlay that draws the current tone-mapping curve over the picture so you can inspect its shape. It is a troubleshooting tool - leave it off for normal viewing.
SettingsHelpTscale: How frame interpolation blends between two real frames along the time axis. It only does anything while frame interpolation is on - otherwise this setting is inert. Oversample is sharper, Mitchell softer.
SettingsHelpUiFont: Font used for the app's menus and interface.
SettingsHelpUnassociateFiles: Remove the media file associations registered by this player.
SettingsHelpUserAgent: User agent used for HTTP streaming. Leave empty for the default.
SettingsHelpVideoDecodeDirect: Decode video frames directly into GPU memory to reduce copies. Auto is recommended; set to Off if you see glitches with some drivers.
SettingsHelpVideoExts: Video extensions recognized when collecting playlist files, comma-separated.
SettingsHelpVideoOutputLevels: Signal range sent to the display. Limited is TV range, Full is PC range.
SettingsHelpVideoPreview: Show video preview thumbnails when hovering the progress bar.
SettingsHelpVideoReversalBuffer: Approximate max bytes buffered for backward decoding; raise if reversal queue overflows.
SettingsHelpVideoZoom: Scales the whole picture. 0 is the original size; combine it with panning below to look at one part of the frame.
SettingsHelpVideoPanX: Moves the picture sideways, as a fraction of its width. Only visible once zoomed in.
SettingsHelpVideoPanY: Moves the picture up or down, as a fraction of its height. Only visible once zoomed in.
SettingsHelpVideoAlignX: Which side the picture sits on when the window is wider than it. -1 left, 0 centred, 1 right.
SettingsHelpVideoAlignY: Which side the picture sits on when the window is taller than it. -1 top, 0 centred, 1 bottom.
SettingsHelpVideoSync: How playback is aligned to the display refresh rate. The default, audio, takes sound as the reference and is the most stable. display-resample nudges playback speed so every refresh gets a new frame - it is a prerequisite for frame interpolation. desync ignores the match entirely.
SettingsHelpVideoSyncMaxVideoChange: Largest playback-speed adjustment allowed while resampling, in percent. Bigger values align more reliably, but past roughly 1% the pitch shift becomes audible.
SettingsHelpVideoUnscaled: Render the video at its original pixel size instead of scaling it to the window.
SettingsHelpVolumeMax: Upper limit of the volume control (%). Values above 100 allow amplifier-style boost.
SettingsHelpVsrAuto: On an NVIDIA card, uses VSR to sharpen low-resolution video automatically. It suits older films, animation and web video, and stacks with RTX Video HDR. It steps aside when another video filter is detected, so they do not fight. Has no effect on other brands.
SettingsHelpWatchLaterDir: Folder where mpv stores resume files. Leave empty for the built-in default.
SettingsHelpWatchLaterOptions: Comma-separated properties saved with the playback position, e.g. start,vid,aid,sid.
SettingsHelpWindowAspectRatioLock: On: the window follows the video aspect ratio — corrected when a video opens and while dragging. Off: resize the window freely.
SettingsHelpWindowPiPSize: Size of the floating mini-player window.
SettingsHelpWindowTitle: Override the window title. Empty uses the media title.
SettingsMetadataOsdAutohideForAudioWithA: Auto-hide metadata OSD for album art audio
SettingsMetadataOsdEnableForAudioWithAlb: Show metadata OSD for album art audio
SettingsResetAllConfirm: Reset all settings to their defaults? This cannot be undone.
SettingsResetConfirm: Reset the settings on this page to their defaults?
SettingsWindowAspectRatioLock: Lock aspect ratio to the video
WarningBlendSubtitlesMargins: Ignored while subtitles are blended into the video frame.
WarningDebandHwdec: May be ineffective with hardware decoding; switch hardware decoding to Off for guaranteed effect.
WarningHrSeekFramedrop: Not recommended while frame interpolation is enabled; disable it to keep interpolation accurate.
WarningInterpolationVideoSync: Only effective with the "Resample to display refresh" video sync mode.
WarningLinearUpscalingSigmoid: Linear light upscaling is enabled; the two options are mutually exclusive.
WarningSaveWithoutResume: Playback resume is disabled, so saved positions will not be restored.
WarningSeekHoldInactive: Both auto VSR and RTX Video HDR are off; this option has no effect.
WarningOverriddenByMpvConf: mpv.conf sets this option, so it overrides this value. Edit it in the mpv.conf [user overrides] block.
WarningSubFallbackNoLanguage: No preferred subtitle language is set, so fallback has no effect.
WarningTscaleInterpolation: Only effective while frame interpolation is enabled.
WatchHistoryClearConfirm: Are you sure you want to clear the history?
WatchHistoryDisabled: Enable --save-watch-history to jump to recently played files.
WatchHistoryEmpty: The watch history file is empty.
